dish: House-made otōshi and home-cooked plates, famously the meat pie
n: Stand Suehiro, Sakaemachi (スタンド末広)
address: Ōyama Apartment 1F, 388-9 Asato, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
w: A small standing-style bar on the edge of Sakaemachi Market, named after the shokudō the owner's grandmother ran in Osaka. OTV's Sakaemachi bar-hop series calls its house-made otōshi the 'strongest' it found, and Smart Magazine singles out the meat pie as the popular order.

dish: Osaka-style kushikatsu (beef kushikatsu is the No.1 order) on a 4-item senbero set
n: Okinawa Kushikatsu Senbero-ya, Sakaemachi (沖縄串カツ せんべろ家)
w: A red-lantern kushikatsu counter inside Sakaemachi Market, sister shop of the bone-broth specialist Honejiru-ya. It fries Osaka-style kushikatsu and runs a 'senbero' set (4 items for ¥1,000); beef kushikatsu is the best seller, and OTV's Sakaemachi bar-hop series also praises its chicken wings.

dish: ¥50 mini croissants (sold in bags of ten) and a counter of sweet, savoury and hard breads
n: BOULANGERIE BZ, Yogi (ブーランジェリービズ)
w: A neighbourhood counter bakery in Yogi where staff fetch the breads you name. Its glazed mini croissants, ¥50 each and sold by the bag, are the famous item and are often reserved a day ahead; RETRIP and the local site TAGOO both list it among Naha's favourite bakeries.
